conventions.convention: Cartier equations multiply under divisor addition; zeros are positive and poles negative. A unit equation represents the zero divisor.
For local equations f_i, O_X(D) is the subsheaf f_i^(-1)O_X of the meromorphic sheaf; for effective D, O_X(-D) is its ideal sheaf.
Effectiveness requires multiplication by every equation germ to be injective. Local principality alone is insufficient; the equation 1 defines the empty effective divisor.
A rational section on an integral scheme is a nonzero meromorphic section. The canonical rational section 1_D need not be a regular global section of O_X(D).

Weil divisors on a normal Noetherian scheme have locally finite support, hence finite support by quasi-compactness. The cycle construction assumes DC; the injectivity and locally factorial comparison assume AC.
A Cartier pullback is defined through admissible fractions whose numerators and denominators pull back to regular sections. Flat morphisms admit every Cartier pullback.

A proper curve is integral, proper over the field, and of chain dimension one; geometric integrality and smoothness are not part of this definition. Degree is the finite sum of coefficients weighted by residue-field degrees.
The finite dominant map associated to a rational function requires transcendence over k. An algebraic nonzero function on a normal proper curve is a global unit, even if it is outside k.

Compact-group Hilbert pairings are linear in the first variable. Haar measure is normalized Borel probability; completeness of the measure is not assumed. Arbitrary bounded operators are averaged weakly.
P_sigma uses the conjugated character and the factor d_sigma. H_sigma is the closed span of sigma-copies; no completeness or sum-over-the-dual assertion is made.
Specht actions are left actions and tabloid rows remain labelled. The integral/modular tabloid form is symmetric bilinear, distinct from the published complex Hermitian form.

p-regular means every positive-part multiplicity is less than p; p-restricted means consecutive padded parts differ by less than p. Conjugation exchanges these conditions. The empty partition is allowed.

D^lambda is initially a form-radical quotient. Its identification as the module head is asserted only when nonzero. Classification and decomposition numbers use a fixed splitting p-modular system, without requiring algebraic closure.

load_bearing.statement: On an integral scheme, a nonzero rational section s of an invertible sheaf L determines a Cartier divisor D and a canonical isomorphism O_X(D) → L carrying the canonical rational section 1_D to s. Conversely div_C(1_D)=D; two pairs have equal divisors exactly when they are isomorphic carrying their rational sections to one another.

Standard polytabloids form a Z-basis of the integral Specht lattice. It is a direct summand of the integral tabloid module; for every commutative ring R, the canonical base-change map is injective onto S^lambda_R. The empty shape has rank one.

For every scheme X, D ↦ [O_X(D)] is a homomorphism CaDiv(X) → Pic(X) with kernel exactly the principal Cartier divisors. If X is integral, it is surjective and induces CaDiv(X)/Prin_C(X) ≅ Pic(X). No choice principle is used.

Assume AC. A locally factorial Noetherian integral scheme is normal; every prime divisor is effective Cartier with cycle [Z], the cycle map is an isomorphism of divisor groups, and the canonical Pic(X) → Cl(X) is an isomorphism.

Assume AC, hence DC. For every normal proper curve C over a field k and every f ∈ k(C)^×, the principal Weil divisor is a finite combination of closed points and its residue-weighted k-degree is zero. No smoothness, projectivity or separability hypothesis is imposed.

For every field F and F[S_n]-submodule U ≤ M^lambda_F, either S^lambda_F ≤ U or U ≤ (S^lambda_F)^⊥. D^lambda_F is zero or absolutely irreducible and is self-dual in either case. When nonzero, its form radical is the unique maximal submodule and module radical of S^lambda_F, and D^lambda_F is its simple head.

For every partition lambda, put L=∏z_j! and U=∏(z_j!)^j. The positive gcd g of all integral polytabloid pairings is also the gcd of the standard Gram entries, and L divides g divides U. For every prime p, p does not divide g exactly when lambda is p-regular. Row reversal gives beta(e_t,e_t*)=U and kappa_t e_t*=U e_t over every field.

Over a field of characteristic p, with lambda p-regular, every nonzero map S^lambda_F → M^mu_F/U forces lambda to dominate mu. For equal shapes its image is (S^mu_F+U)/U and U does not contain S^mu_F. The same holds for D^lambda_F; isomorphic nonzero James quotients have equal labels.

Assume AC. For a strongly continuous unitary representation of a compact Hausdorff group on nonzero H and nonzero xi, the conjugation orbit of R_xi is norm-continuous and Bochner integrable. Its average is bounded, positive, self-adjoint, nonzero, compact, and commutes with the representation.

Assume AC. Matrix coefficients of inequivalent irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of a compact Hausdorff group are orthogonal for normalized Haar probability. For one irreducible of degree d, their integral pairing is d^(-1)⟨v,v'⟩ conjugate(⟨w,w'⟩), with first-variable-linear pairings; unitary-equivalent models satisfy the corresponding transported formula.

Assume AC. P_sigma is bounded, linear, self-adjoint and equivariant, fixes every sigma-copy, is idempotent, and has range exactly H_sigma. Inequivalent types give products zero in both orders and orthogonal ranges. No completeness, density or Peter–Weyl statement is used.

concerns.concern: [F4] says that for an arbitrary Cartier divisor, 'the constant meromorphic function 1 is a global section of O_X(D)'. This changes a rational section into a regular global section. For X=Spec k[t] and D=-[0], O_X(D)=tO_X and 1 is not a global section. The Statement and final example correctly distinguish these notions.

[F9] asserts that a local Artinian ring S with residue field lambda satisfies length_S(S)=dim_lambda S; step 1.3 invokes this. No lambda-vector-space structure on S is supplied, and a coefficient field compatible with the given base field need not exist. Neither cited item states this assertion. The preceding filtration by residue-field factors does establish the required k-dimension formula.

Statement 3 says d_(lambda,mu)=0 when mu is 'strictly larger than lambda in decreasing lexicographic order'. [F10] and step 4.1 use precisely that phrase for mu strictly dominating lambda, where entries are allowed to be nonzero. The assigned S3 example has d_((2,1),(3))=1 at p=3. Separately, [F1] asserts S^lambda_R is nonzero for every commutative ring R, which fails for the zero ring.

Step 2.1 says '[2]' has a single column of height 2 and '(1,1)' has two columns of height 1. These descriptions are reversed: (2) has two height-one columns, while (1,1) has one height-two column. The displayed conjugation equalities and the counterexample's conclusion are correct.

[F2] states, after quantifying over every commutative ring R, that 'all elements are integral combinations of standard polytabloids'. Arbitrary elements after base change require R-coefficients. For a characteristic-p field containing alpha outside its prime field, alpha e_t cannot generally be an integer combination of the standard basis. The supplier proves integral combinations for integral polytabloids.

[F2] asserts 'e_t≠0 over every coefficient ring'. The zero ring is allowed in the base-change supplier and gives the zero module and zero polytabloids. Nonvanishing over the fields in this lemma's Statement is valid.

[F1] quantifies over every commutative ring R and concludes e_t≠0 from its coefficient 1. For R=0 that coefficient is zero and e_t=0. The theorem over fields is unaffected, but the stated general-ring fact is false.

[F1] concludes e_t≠0 for every commutative coefficient ring R. Taking R=0 contradicts this assertion. The field-level criterion and its Gram argument do not require this overstrong general-ring claim.

Step 2.1 writes sigma·(e_t0⊗w)=(sigma·e_t0)⊗w, omitting sgn(sigma) from the declared diagonal action. In odd characteristic, an odd permutation supplies a direct counterexample to this equality. The spanning argument remains available because the omitted scalar is a unit.

[F5] and step 1.1 assert ||c^(-1)I_H||=|c|^(-1), but H=0 is permitted and its operator norm is 0. Also step 1.2 proves only sequential closedness before claiming closedness in a choice-free argument; norm continuity directly proves the needed closedness without a sequential-closure principle. The main finite-dimensionality conclusion includes H=0 and is true.

[F4] states without qualification that operator norm is the supremum over the unit sphere. H=0 is allowed, so this sphere is empty; the opened def-operator-norm explicitly restricts that formula to nonzero domain and uses the unit-ball formula otherwise.

[F10] calls integrality equivalent to being 'a nonempty scheme covered by spectra of domains'. A disjoint union of two field spectra satisfies that condition but is not integral. The opened def-integral-scheme instead requires every nonempty affine open to have a domain coordinate ring, or reducedness and irreducibility. This example's single affine domain does establish its own integrality.

In step 1.1, the branch where c is a unit replaces ab=pi c by pi=p_1⋯p_m q_1⋯q_n, dropping c^(-1). The argument needs unit-adjusted factors or the immediate irreducibility contradiction in this branch.

Step 1.2 invokes 'A union of two irreducible spaces with nonempty intersection is irreducible'. This is false without further hypotheses, as two intersecting closed lines show. Here the two charts are open, and their nonempty intersection is dense in each; those stated chart properties supply the short valid argument.
[F3] prints cyc:K(X)^×→Div(X) while immediately applying cyc to arbitrary Cartier divisors D and E. The cited supplier's cycle map has domain CaDiv(X); the function-domain map is div_W.

[F7] cites thm-composition-of-continuous-functions for composition of maps between general topological spaces. That opened theorem is restricted to real functions on subsets of R. The needed general result is elementary and is explicitly stated in the also-opened lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes.

Step 1.7 cites future step 2.1, whose conclusion itself cites step 1.7. The degree computation has independent support in the preceding order and residue-degree calculations, so this forward/circular justification tag is unnecessary.

alerts.finding: [F4] begins 'The current Cartier interfaces define the sheaf and linear-equivalence conventions' and continues with a summary of six suppliers' roles. This does not state their exact propositions as the seam task requires. The inspected proof does apply the integral and locally factorial interfaces with the appropriate curve and choice hypotheses; the alert concerns the summary-style fact citation.

[F7] says the interfaces 'define the pullback Cartier divisor and identify its associated sheaf with the pulled-back line bundle', without stating the defined-pullback hypothesis of lem-pullback-cartier-divisor-line-bundle. Step 5.1 separately establishes flatness through [F9], so the inspected application is valid; the fact should state the actual conditional proposition.

[F6] attributes to thm-principal-divisor-degree-zero-proper-curve the assertion that a principal divisor 'on a proper curve has degree 0'. The opened supplier assumes AC and a normal proper curve. The present smooth curve with standing AC meets those conditions, but the citation as worded drops normality and overstates the supplier's domain.

[F4] states 'Principal divisors on a proper curve have degree zero' and cites thm-principal-divisor-degree-zero-proper-curve. The supplier states this for normal proper curves under AC. Those hypotheses hold in the present smooth-curve context, but are absent from the quoted fact.
